title: Facebook Sets Two-Year Suspension for Trump
description_short: Meta said Trump’s suspension would last two years, with reinstatement conditioned on safety assessments.
description_medium: Facebook set a two-year suspension for Trump after its Oversight Board reviewed the earlier indefinite ban. The company said a return would depend on safety assessments. The decision gave the suspension a defined term while leaving reinstatement conditional, rather than promising that Trump would automatically regain access when the two years ended.
description_long:
Facebook set a two-year suspension for Donald Trump after the Oversight Board reviewed the platform's earlier decision to block him indefinitely. The supplied record says the company conditioned reinstatement on safety assessments. This replaced an open-ended suspension with a stated duration while retaining a separate question about whether a return would be safe.

The distinction between a suspension period and automatic reinstatement is central to the announcement. A two-year term described how long the restriction would initially last; it did not guarantee that access would resume regardless of conditions. The company reserved an assessment of the risks before restoring the account.

The decision was a platform-governance action affecting Trump's ability to communicate through Facebook, rather than a governmental restriction on his speech. The supplied material supports the duration, the Oversight Board context, and the conditional nature of a possible return. It does not give the complete assessment criteria, establish the eventual reinstatement decision, or quantify the suspension's effect on his political audience.

description_long:
Truth Social became available through Google's Play Store after earlier concerns about moderation delayed approval. The supplied record says the app gained Android distribution after meeting Google's content policies. The event concerns access to a major app marketplace, rather than the creation of the social network or a change in government regulation.

Marketplace approval matters because it provides a distribution route through which users can obtain an application. In this case, the earlier delay connected that access to Google's requirements for handling content. Approval indicated that the app had met the applicable marketplace conditions described in the supplied account; it did not amount to Google's endorsement of every post or the platform's political positions.

The supported account does not identify all moderation changes, the full sequence of negotiations, or the number of users who joined because of the approval. It also does not show that any earlier concerns were permanently resolved. The immediate result was availability in the Play Store after the prior content-policy obstacle.
